_note: An illustrative schedule for the timeline. The model assumes only twelve years of works with even spending (params.build_years); the split of those years between tasks and stages is an assumption made for this page, not a programme. Staging itself is a study point. Each corridor lists its twin-track tunnels by kind of train (tgv, n = RER G, h = RER F; there is no regional express tunnel since version 4.1, the regional express trains share the TGV tunnels and 'ter' marks the corridors where they do, as model.ter_corridors); their lengths come from model.json (corridor_km, link_km), and the page checks that they add up to cost.tunnel_km and to the km of each stage.

network.text: Every train ends in Paris. Changing from one line to another means crossing the city by metro or RER.

TGVs from the north, the east and the south-east run through Paris Nord-Est and Gare de Lyon, and some run straight through Paris. RER F runs from the northern suburbs through Nord-Est and Saint-Lazare to the west. Atlantic TGVs, the regional express trains and lines P and N still end at their terminals: no through train reaches the Atlantic, and the link is not open.

The four TGV lines are joined in a triangle: every TGV stops at two stations, and TGVs between the Atlantic and the south-east take the link. Regional express trains share the TGV tunnels: those of the north run through Nord-Est to Montparnasse and the Atlantic lines, those of the east through Nord-Est to Gare de Lyon and Burgundy, and none turns back in Paris. RER G joins the east to the south-west. Only line R keeps a small surface terminal at Gare de Lyon.

seen.name: Gare du Nord and Gare de l’Est

phases.text: Two terminals, 500 m apart.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear on railway land beside the approach tracks. Some entrances and passages are moved.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are shortened or closed in turn above the works, and some trains leave from other platforms.

The TGV and RER F platforms below are complete; empty trains run through them. New ways down appear in the two halls, still closed. The control hall for London trains is fitted out on the Gare du Nord side.

TGVs and RER F trains leave from the deep platforms; London trains board from a TGV platform closed off for each departure. Their surface platforms close. Regional express trains and line P still use the surface while their own platforms are built below, on the west side of the box.

One station with two halls. Every train now runs below, the regional express trains in the TGV tunnels, so all the surface tracks of both stations close and are cleared; the park on their site can open some years later (assumption).
A terminal on two levels: main-line trains above, RER below.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear beside the tracks towards Bercy.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works. The junction cavern for the later link is dug with the station.
Empty TGVs run through the station below. New ways down appear in the hall, still closed.

TGVs leave from the deep platforms and continue to Paris Nord-Est; the two new tracks take the sixteenth south-eastern TGV an hour. Their surface platforms close and the hall is refitted. The regional express trains, line R and the Bercy trains keep the surface until the regional express platforms of Nord-Est open (assumption). The link is joined to the junction cavern from inside, without closing the station.

The hall is the entrance; half the TGVs continue to Montparnasse by the link. The regional express trains of Gare de Lyon and Bercy run below, through to Nord-Est, so the Bercy station and most surface tracks close; line R keeps a small terminal of a few tracks. The park comes some years later.
A terminal for suburban lines J and L and the trains to Normandy.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear on railway land in the station and towards Pont-Cardinet.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works.
Empty RER F trains run through the station below, between Nord-Est and the west.
RER F trains, which now include those of line L, run through the deep station between Nord-Est and the west. The surface station stays for line J and the trains to Normandy.
A terminal with platforms one level above the street.
Nothing changes yet.
Trains run as today. Work sites appear beside the approach tracks.
Trains run, with fewer platforms at a time. A few platforms are closed in turn above the works. The junction cavern for the link is dug with the station.

All Atlantic trains, regional express trains and line N still end here on the surface, while RER F and three of the TGV lines are already open below. Below, the station and the tunnels are being fitted out.
Empty trains run through the station below, towards Paris Nord-Est and over the link to Gare de Lyon. New ways down appear in the hall, still closed.

TGVs leave from the deep platforms, half to Paris Nord-Est and half to Gare de Lyon by the link; regional express trains run through to Nord-Est in the TGV tunnel, and RER G in its own. The surface platforms and the tracks to the ring road close; the park comes later.
